evals.prompt: Author verification acceptance for a small batch-import CLI change. Required outcomes: successful single-item and multi-item imports produce correct durable results, accurate summaries, and clean temporary files; malformed records and forbidden destinations are rejected without altering durable data; cancellation while the real process is writing leaves no partial published result. Existing deterministic public-seam tests already cover parser boundaries and destination authorization. An isolated filesystem-level integration fixture can observe rejection and unchanged durable data. Successful result, summary, and cleanup are compatible observations in one CLI journey. Signal delivery and cancellation cleanup must be observed through the real CLI process and cannot be established by static source inspection or the parser tests. A proposed draft assigns a separate full CLI end-to-end scenario to each requirement and input variation. Produce concise Behavior/Check acceptance and the material proof-selection rationale; preserve every required outcome and identify which observations can share a run. Assume standard assurance and no permission to weaken independent verification. Do not implement or execute the fictional CLI.
evals.expected_output: Preserve every single-item, multi-item, summary, cleanup, rejection, durable-data, and cancellation obligation in exact Behavior/Check acceptance. Combine compatible successful CLI observations, reuse existing adequate public-seam proof and focused filesystem rejection proof, and separately observe cancellation through the real process. Explain otherwise-unproved behavior for additional expensive execution without imposing a count cap or reduction percentage. Independent verification still freshly executes the approved complete set; do not claim the fictional CLI ran.
assertions: Every required outcome remains explicitly checkable with an exact expected observation
Compatible successful result, summary, and cleanup observations share proof rather than mechanically creating full journeys per requirement
Existing parser and authorization coverage and adequate focused rejection proof are used instead of redundant full journeys
Cancellation remains separately observed through the real CLI process, not source inspection or parser tests
Additional expensive scenarios explain their otherwise-unproved behavior and cheaper-proof insufficiency without a numeric cap
Independent complete verification and acceptance authority remain unchanged, with no invented execution

evals.prompt: Author a technical specification from settled requirements for a repository-only migration. The candidate must choose implementation boundaries and concrete proof, and an applicable canonical contract is current. Work inline in one author: resolve the current requirements, canonical contract, task-sizing guidance, and proof-selection guidance before drafting; then, only after a substantive candidate exists, apply the installed planning rethink once before the final Handoff. Preserve product behavior and assurance, make at most one correction to technical decisions owned by specification, and execute no fictional application checks.
evals.expected_output: A revision-bound specification whose trace distinguishes current-source resolution, initial candidate, one same-author post-candidate planning rethink, any single bounded correction, and final Handoff. Product behavior, effects, assurance, and downstream ticket ownership remain outside the specification author's correction authority. No new stage, ledger, plan field, or invented runtime evidence appears.
assertions: Applicable current authority, canonical, sizing, and proof sources are resolved before the initial candidate rather than reconstructed from memory
The same specification author performs one explicit planning rethink only after a substantive candidate and before the final Handoff
Any correction is bounded to specification-owned technical decisions and preserves confirmed behavior, effects, and assurance
The result adds no planning stage or state and claims no fictional execution

evals.prompt: Author a standard-assurance technical specification inline. Implementation owners run their owned acceptance checks before handing off; after all handoffs come one independent review and then one independent verifier that freshly runs the complete acceptance set; the controller schedules and validates only and never edits files. The initial candidate gives one implementation task an expensive end-to-end acceptance item driven by a disposable driver that task creates; the task runs it before handing off, the verifier repeats it with the same driver, and the task's owner removes the driver after verification. During the one planning rethink, cost pressure suggests running the end-to-end item only once in verification and having the controller delete the driver. Apply the installed planning rethink once and return the final specification.
evals.expected_output: The final specification keeps the implementation-owned end-to-end run before handoff plus the verifier's fresh repetition, and keeps driver cleanup with the task owner after verification. The verifier-only reduction and the controller cleanup are rejected as lifecycle-invalid, not as generic cost aversion.
assertions: No implementation handoff depends on a check that only a later verification role can run
Cleanup of the task-created driver stays with an owner whose role permits editing and who exists when cleanup is due, not the non-editing controller
The independent verifier still freshly runs the complete acceptance set
The rethink makes at most one bounded correction and adds no stage, gate, field, or ledger

evals.prompt: Author a standard-assurance technical specification inline whose initial candidate has three simplifiable choices: a task deletes its disposable end-to-end driver before handing off although the verifier needs the same driver; two separate full journeys with identical setup each prove one of two compatible acceptance items; and a separate task only reruns another task's unit suite while owning no acceptance item. Apply the installed planning rethink once and return the final specification.
evals.expected_output: The final specification keeps the driver unchanged through handoff, review, and verification with removal by its original owner afterwards; combines the two compatible observations into one journey that records each exact expected result; and removes the task that owns no obligation. Lifecycle checks do not block these simplifications.
assertions: A task-created artifact may outlive its creator's handoff when a later role needs it, with removal assigned to its original owner after that role
One shared scenario may establish several compatible acceptance items when each keeps its exact expected observation
A task that owns no obligation and only repeats another owner's check is removed without losing any responsibility, independence boundary, or prerequisite
Verification still freshly runs the complete acceptance set

evals.prompt: The current approved technical specification is supplied byte-for-byte and needs only an unchanged forwarding Handoff to its existing next owner. Make no technical, boundary, proof, authority, or effect decision. Preserve the artifact exactly; do not perform a new planning rethink merely because it is being forwarded.
evals.expected_output: The unchanged approved specification is forwarded through the existing Handoff procedure without a planning-rethink pass, correction, new approval, or rewritten acceptance.
assertions: An exact unchanged approved specification projection does not trigger planning rethink
The existing authority, acceptance, route, and Handoff destination remain unchanged
No new stage, approval gate, or author-owned decision is invented
